sections.heading: Why Windows Fog Up and Why It Matters
sections.body: Foggy windows occur when the hermetic seal surrounding an insulated glass unit (IGU) breaks down. Modern double- and triple-pane windows are manufactured with inert gas — typically argon or krypton — sealed between the panes to act as a thermal barrier. Over time, temperature cycling, UV exposure, and normal building movement stress the seal until it fails. Once air and humidity infiltrate the gap, condensation forms on the interior glass surfaces and cannot be wiped away from the outside. The result is permanent fogging that reduces natural light transmission, increases solar heat gain in summer, eliminates the insulating gas layer, and raises heating and cooling costs year-round. For property managers overseeing office buildings near Rosslyn's skyline corridor or homeowners in quiet Bluemont neighborhoods, a failed IGU is not a cosmetic problem to ignore — it is an ongoing energy drain that compounds every month it goes unaddressed.

sections.heading: Our Foggy Window Repair and IGU Replacement Process
sections.body: Our technicians begin every job with a thorough inspection to determine whether the seal failure is isolated to a single pane or part of a broader pattern affecting multiple units. In many cases, we can replace only the failed insulated glass unit rather than the entire window frame, saving you significant cost. We source high-quality tempered, laminated, or low-e glass to match your existing window specifications precisely. Once the new IGU is fabricated and delivered, our crew removes the damaged pane, cleans the frame and glazing channels, installs the new unit with fresh glazing compound or structural silicone, and verifies a watertight seal before leaving the job site. For commercial clients managing multi-story buildings along the Wilson Boulevard corridor in Ballston, we coordinate scheduling to minimize disruption to tenants and daily operations. Every repair is backed by our commitment to licensed, insured workmanship.

faq.q: Can foggy windows be repaired without replacing the entire window frame?
faq.a: Yes. In most cases only the insulated glass unit itself needs to be replaced, not the surrounding frame. This approach is significantly less expensive and produces results that look identical to a full window replacement.

faq.q: How long does a foggy window repair take?
faq.a: Most residential IGU replacements are completed in a single visit lasting one to three hours per window. Commercial projects with multiple units may require additional time, and we will provide a clear timeline during the estimate process.

faq.q: Does foggy window repair improve energy efficiency?
faq.a: Absolutely. A failed IGU loses its insulating gas fill, dramatically reducing the window's R-value. Replacing the unit restores the thermal barrier, which lowers heating and cooling costs and improves interior comfort year-round.
